regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY is the headline; IIP YoY at 6.7% YoY (down from 8.8% YoY prior) and core sector at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0% YoY) are the reality check. PMI composite at 54.6 index holds, but manufacturing PMI slipped to 52.8 index while services at 54.5 index carries the load — a services-led expansion is inherently harder to sustain when fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY is compressing household discretionary budgets. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is the one genuinely encouraging number: it is above the 75% threshold that historically precedes private capex commitment, but the inversion to watch is whether credit-funded capex is pulling forward demand that deposit growth cannot support.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"CPI headline at 4.45% YoY looks manageable until you decompose it: food at 5.52% YoY, fuel at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, a 3-month high), and core CPI at 3.9% YoY. The gap between fuel and core is the tell — fuel is a cost-push shock that feeds into transport, logistics, and manufacturing margins within two quarters, eventually lifting core even as the RBI waits. WPI at 9.92% YoY confirms the pipeline pressure. RBI has already revised its inflation forecast to 5.1% YoY from 4.6% YoY; with repo at 5.25% p.a., the real rate is 15bps — insufficient to anchor a currency depreciating at a 91st-percentile 96.15 ₹.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth at 10.8% YoY is a 630bps divergence that the CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile historically) only partially captures. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% YoY signals wholesale funding demand is rising precisely when the deposit base is thinning. The last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% during a rate-hold cycle, the regulator responded with risk-weight tightening on unsecured lending — the incentive structure for banks (fee income, market share) pushes them to grow credit regardless, which is exactly when macro-prudential tools arrive uninvited. Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (0th percentile) suggests the capital market is not absorbing the slack.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. (38th percentile) is on extended hold, but the RBI's own inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY makes the real rate 15bps — a number that does no heavy lifting on currency defence or inflation anchoring. The policy dilemma is structural: cut and the INR at 96.15 ₹ (91st percentile) depreciates further, widening the import bill on Brent at $97.56 / bbl; hold and credit-deposit stress compounds. The RBI is not driving with one foot on each pedal by choice — it is trapped between a fuel shock it cannot control and a currency it cannot afford to abandon.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile, up from 75.6% prior) make the capex upcycle case look compelling. Bank credit to industry at 20.0% YoY (up from 6.5% YoY prior) and to services at 22.9% YoY (up from 10.2% YoY prior) confirm financing is flowing. The inversion: office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (6th percentile, a 10-year low) is the leading indicator for GCC and IT-sector capex commitments — if the largest occupier class is contracting its footprint, the services credit surge may be financing working capital and refinancing, not new productive capacity.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month (71st percentile) and passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY, two-wheeler at 19.7% YoY, and commercial vehicles at 16.88% YoY paint a broad-based demand picture. But GST must be interrogated: at ₹1,99,853 cr / month, how much is genuine volume growth versus price-level effects from 22.93% YoY fuel inflation lifting nominal transaction values? Two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY are the most reliable mass-consumption proxy — this segment is rural and semi-urban, suggesting the informal economy is participating. The risk: fuel at 22.93% YoY is a direct tax on two-wheeler commuters; if it sustains, the next print will tell you whether demand is durable or front-loaded.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (latest, down from 82.5% prior) remains elevated at 75th percentile historically. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (latest, up from 10.6% prior) signals wholesale funding pressure mounting.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; they face margin compression and refinancing risk. RBI will likely ease liquidity via OMOs or CRR cuts within 2-3 months if deposit growth doesn't accelerate. Position for a 25-50 bps rate cut by Q3 FY27.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile has historically preceded either deposit acceleration or RBI liquidity injections. Last time CD ratio was this elevated (2022), RBI cut CRR by 50 bps within 6 weeks.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadening Across Sectors","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals strong investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (latest, up from 75.6% prior) — at 74th percentile — indicates headroom for capex without overcapacity risk. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (latest, down from 6.0% prior) remains steady. Credit to industry at 20.0% YoY (latest, up from 6.5% prior) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (latest, up from 10.2% prior) show broad-based capex financing.","implication":"Overweight capital goods manufacturers, cement, and steel. Accumulate infrastructure plays (roads, ports, power) — order books will fill through H2 FY27. Private capex is now the growth engine; public capex is moderating. Avoid low-utilisation sectors (textiles, auto components) until capacity utilisation breaches 80%.","pct_10y":52,"pct_note":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% is above the 10-year median; capacity utilisation at 77.4% is mid-range, suggesting capex cycle is mid-stage, not overheated. This level has historically sustained for 8-12 quarters.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Retail Equity Inflows Hit Record Highs","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (latest, up from ₹31,961 cr / month prior) — rising 2 consecutive months and at 92nd percentile. SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (latest, up from ₹18.21 lakh cr prior) — at 93rd percentile. MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (latest, up from ₹85.76 lakh cr prior) — at 86th percentile. DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr net / month (latest, up from ₹35,099 cr net / month prior) — at 100th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months.","implication":"Retail equity positioning is at decade highs. Reduce equity allocation; rotate into defensive sectors (pharma, FMCG, utilities). Expect volatility if FII flows reverse or global rates spike. Lock in gains on high-beta names.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile preceded market corrections in 2018 and 2022. When retail reaches this saturation, mean reversion typically follows within 6-9 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI Credibility","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest, up from 20.05% prior) — at 95th percentile, a 3-month high. WPI at 9.92% YoY (latest, up from 9.78% prior) — at 67th percentile. Brent crude at $97.56 / bbl (latest, flat) — at 69th percentile. India's import bill for oil and gas is rising; CAD pressure building. RBI inflation forecast revised up to 5.1% YoY (latest, from 4.6% prior).","implication":"RBI will struggle to cut rates if fuel inflation stays > 20%. Expect CPI to reaccelerate to 4.8-5.2% by Q3 FY27, forcing RBI to hold or hike. Underweight refiners (margin compression) and overweight oil explorers (ONGC, Vedanta). Hedge INR weakness — oil imports will widen CAD. Avoid rate-sensitive sectors (NBFCs, auto finance) until inflation trajectory clarifies.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a 10-year extreme. Last time fuel inflation exceeded 20%, RBI kept rates on hold for 18+ months despite growth slowdown.","is_surprise":false}

signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Accelerates Despite RBI Intervention","data_text":"INR/USD at ₹96.15 (latest, up from ₹95.73 prior) — at 91st percentile, a 10-year weak level. INR has depreciated 3 of last 5 periods. India VIX at 10.345 index (latest, flat) — at 5th percentile, falling 5 consecutive periods, indicating complacency. FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month (latest, up from ₹20,200 cr net / month prior) — at 83rd percentile, but volatile (recent: -114 → -3,111.9 → +29,631). Gold in INR at ₹13,354 / g (latest, up from ₹13,295 prior) — at 100th percentile.","implication":"INR weakness is structural, not cyclical. Expect INR to test ₹97-98 by Q2 FY27 if oil stays > $95 / bbl. Hedge INR exposure; overweight exporters (IT, pharma, textiles). Avoid rupee-denominated debt; prefer USD-linked returns. Monitor FII flows closely — any reversal will accelerate INR depreciation.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile weakness has historically preceded 200+ bps depreciation cycles. Last time INR was this weak (2022), it fell another 8% over 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, down from 13.7 mn sq ft / quarter prior) — at 6th percentile, a 10-year low. Recent trend: 29.9 → 21.5 → 26.9 → 48 → 29.9 → 26.9 → 13.2 (collapsing in latest period). Retail mall vacancy at 5.7% vacant (latest, down from 7.5% prior) — at 11th percentile but improving, falling 2 of last 5 periods. Nifty IT index flat at 23,446.8 (latest, up 4 of last 5 periods). Airline passenger traffic at 86.4 mn / month (latest, up from 85.17 mn / month prior) — at 35th percentile, mild-negative signal.","implication":"Office absorption collapse is NOT an IT services crisis — it's a structural shift to GCC (Global Capability Centers) and hybrid work. Traditional IT services firms (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are consolidating real estate; GCCs (Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Apple) are the marginal buyer but at lower per-sqft rates. Retail mall recovery (5.7% vacancy) shows consumer discretionary is healthy. IMPLICATION: Overweight IT services on valuation (P/E compression unwarranted) but underweight commercial real estate REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) — they face 15-20% NAV compression as office rents normalize downward. Airline traffic at 35th percentile suggests business travel is NOT recovering; this confirms GCC shift away from traditional IT hubs. FALSIFIABILITY: If office absorption rebounds to > 20 mn sq ft / quarter AND airline pax accelerates to > 90 mn / month, then traditional IT services capex is recovering and this thesis breaks.","pct_10y":6,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 6th percentile is a 10-year extreme low. This level has historically preceded 18-24 months of structural real estate repricing, not cyclical recovery. Retail mall vacancy improving (11th percentile) while office collapses is a rare divergence — it signals sector rotation, not broad weakness.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Services Carry Growth — Fuel Threatens to Reprice Everything

The facts:

  • PMI composite at 54.6 index (83rd percentile) holds, but manufacturing PMI slipped to 52.8 index while services at 54.5 index does the lifting.
  • IIP YoY at 6.7% YoY, down from 8.8% YoY prior; core sector at 5.4% YoY, down from 6.0% YoY — goods economy decelerating beneath the composite.
  • Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile) crossed the 75% threshold that historically precedes private capex commitment.
  • But fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) compresses household budgets and feeds into logistics costs within two quarters — the same quarters the capex upcycle needs to sustain.

The tension: GDP at 7.8% YoY is services-led and statistically clean; the goods economy — IIP, core sector — is losing momentum. Fuel at 22.93% YoY is the variable that can unwind both the consumption story and the capex story simultaneously.

Bottom line: Watch two-wheeler sales as the rural demand stress-test: a print below 15% YoY in the next cycle would signal fuel is biting the informal economy.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Surveys Signal Re-Acceleration — Nominal GDP Says Otherwise

The facts:

  • US PMI composite at 56 index (84th percentile) and Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,299.82 index (100th percentile) price a growth re-acceleration.
  • But US GDP SAAR slowed to 1.5% SAAR from 2.1% SAAR; China GDP at 4.3% YoY (down from 5.0% YoY) with PMI composite at 49.5 index — contraction territory.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% yield (90th percentile) is tightening financial conditions for the Fed; BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, a 10-year high) is unwinding yen carry.
  • DXY at 101.178 index rising 4 of last 5 periods — dollar strength compounds EM currency pressure, including INR at 96.15 ₹.

The tension: Survey data prices re-acceleration; nominal GDP and China's PMI price deceleration. Bond markets are tightening for the Fed without a rate move — the real economy is already absorbing the cost.

Bottom line: BOJ is the underappreciated tail risk: each 25bps hike unwinds carry positions that have funded EM equity inflows, including India's FII flows at ₹29,631 cr net / month.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Liquidity at Record Depth — Deposit Base Is the Fault Line

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile), rising 2 consecutive months; SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile).
  • DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile), rising 2 consecutive months — domestic absorption at a structural high.
  • FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month (83rd percentile), but the recent sequence — ₹-114 → ₹-3,111.9 → ₹29,631 cr net / month — signals volatility, not conviction.
  • But bank deposit growth at 10.8% YoY against credit at 17.1% YoY means the system's funding base is not keeping pace with its lending ambition.

The tension: Equity liquidity is at cycle highs; banking system liquidity is structurally strained. SIP flows sustain market depth, but they do not solve the deposit gap that is tightening NBFC funding costs.

Bottom line: If NBFC credit growth at 14.9% YoY continues accelerating while corporate bond issuance stays at its 0th-percentile ₹18,700 cr / month, a macro-prudential circular on risk weights is the next catalyst to price.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at 93rd Percentile — Office Absorption at 6th Percentile

The facts:

  • Bank Nifty at 56,548.9 index (93rd percentile), rising 3 of last 5 sessions, prices a credit upcycle.
  • But office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (6th percentile, a 10-year low) — the leading indicator for GCC and IT-sector expansion — is at a decade nadir.
  • Office REITs confirm the signal: Embassy REIT at ₹369.92 / unit (down from ₹437.44 / unit prior), Mindspace at ₹345.06 / unit (down from ₹504.76 / unit prior).
  • Residential demand holds: home loan disbursements at ₹4,20,900 cr / quarter (65th percentile) and retail mall vacancy at 5.7% vacant (11th percentile, improving).

The tension: Bank Nifty prices a broad credit and capex upcycle; office absorption at a 10-year low says the largest corporate occupier class is contracting — a leading indicator that services credit growth may be refinancing, not expanding.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until absorption recovers above 20 mn sq ft / quarter; residential and retail real estate remain the better-positioned sub-sectors.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Risks, One Trigger — Fuel Is the Common Thread

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) forces RBI's hand: hold rates and the INR at 96.15 ₹ (91st percentile) depreciates further; cut and imported inflation accelerates — probability high, impact high.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) with NBFC credit at 14.9% YoY accelerating: macro-prudential tightening via risk weights is the historical response — probability medium-high, impact medium.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile): further hikes unwind yen carry, reversing FII flows that swung from ₹-3,111.9 to ₹29,631 cr net / month in a single period — probability medium, impact high.
  • India VIX at 10.345 index (5th percentile), falling 5 consecutive periods: complacency at this level historically precedes a volatility event within 4–6 weeks — probability medium, impact medium.

The tension: The four risks are not independent: a BOJ hike triggers FII outflows, weakens INR, widens the oil import bill, and forces RBI into a tightening posture that the CD ratio cannot absorb without NBFC stress.

Bottom line: Watch RBI's next liquidity management circular: any mention of risk-weight revision on NBFC or unsecured lending is the signal that the credit-deposit stress has crossed the regulator's threshold.

"}
